subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: What exact scope and acceptance criteria should define the native-Linux reasoning-latency investigation before any docs or instrumentation PR is attempted?
rationale: The request is valid and aligned with performance priorities, but the repository evidence shows partial component signals rather than one obvious broken code path, so maintainers need to choose the measurement environment and the minimum useful report shape.

options.title: Scope a runbook first
options.body: Define a bounded CPX32/native-Linux tracing runbook and require layer-by-layer measurements or estimates before optimizing individual hot paths.

options.title: Split by subsystem now
options.body: Open narrower issues for context assembly, memory search, compaction, Telegram, hooks, and auth fallback, accepting more triage overhead but smaller fix boundaries.

options.title: Route to broader performance backlog
options.body: Treat this as supporting context for existing event-loop and diagnostics work, but leave this specific analysis request unsatisfied until a maintainer sponsors it.

recommendation.title: Scope a runbook first
recommendation.body: Define a bounded CPX32/native-Linux tracing runbook and require layer-by-layer measurements or estimates before optimizing individual hot paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current-main routing signal across the docs, observability, and embedded-runner surfaces that frame this investigation.
